text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bunds wavered, then steadied as March U.S. non-farm payrolls rose 175,000 while average hourly earnings rose to $12.5 from $12.10. The market had forecast a 196,000 payroll gain. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.38, up 0.14 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts kept their head and closed 1/4 up despite a negative reaction from U.S. Treasures after jobs data. Traders said the market was very dull, although a general reluctance to sell suggests good support and chance of better performance next week. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-22/32, up 09/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - June bond futures slip from highs after hourly earnings rise in US jobs report rattles traders. Short covering after data pushed contract to high then overseas declines and dealers going short ahead of receiving non-competitive OAT allocations weighed, traders said. Franc steady, PIBOR up. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.08 down 0.01 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets ending up with sudden short covering spur to futures after cash closed, dealers say. Futures now 130 bps up and testing resistance at 126.00 but some traders say there's no tangible reason for such marked strength today except for short squeeze. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.95 up 1.33 from Thursday's settlement price.
